pr_title: ansible-galaxy - fall back to galaxy.yml when listing collections
pr_body:
##### SUMMARY
Fixes #67490
Supersedes #67630

Use galaxy.yml as a fallback for `ansible-galaxy collection list` if the collection doesn't contain a MANIFEST.json file.

##### ISSUE TYPE
- Bugfix Pull Request

issue_context.title: ansible-galaxy collection list should examine galaxy.yml for information

comments:
We could also extend this logic to verify ...

```
(ansible_base) [vagrant@centos8 ~]$ ansible-galaxy collection verify -s http://sivel.eng.ansible.com/api openstack.cloud
[WARNING]: Collection at '/home/vagrant/.ansible/collections/ansible_collections/openstack/cloud' does not have a MANIFEST.json file, cannot detect version.
openstack.cloud has the version '*' but is being compared to '1.0.0'
```

@jctanner I'm not sure if it should work, for verify at least. All built and then published collections should have a MANIFEST (they are built from the galaxy.yml), so it only shouldn't exist after installation if it has been actively deleted or if the collection wasn't built with `ansible-galaxy collection build` and something janky is happening instead. (Also note that galaxy.yml doesn't exist after installation - and since verify is verifying installations...)

But I think the error should be fixed for `verify` since it's misleading.
Fixing the error message for `verify` in https://github.com/ansible/ansible/pull/67498.
This makes sense for `collection list`. We can just fall back to inspecting the local `galaxy.yml` file favoring `MANIFEST.json`. There's already a method to ingest that file, so I can use that.
@samdoran - Would the fix also apply to operations like `ansible-galaxy collection install`?
@geerlingguy The fix just applies to `list`. Does it make sense to apply to `install`, since the collection artifacts should be built before installation?

@s-hertel - Most of the roles I use with ansible (which may be placed inside a collection) are local to a playbook, and don't ever get built or published anywhere. The idea is that I would be able to create a local collection and start using it—it would be a lot of hassle to try to create a collection, publish it somewhere, then install it locally again, just to use it in one local playbook.

@geerlingguy That makes sense, the build + install pattern may be more useful for collections that are published somewhere. (Note that you can install from locally built collections though - no publishing is necessary to create an artifact)

Getting warnings for the local collections while you're trying to install other collections does seem like a bug. What if you have a local collection `namespace.name` that is in the collections path (but wasn't built + installed) and you try to `ansible-galaxy collection install namespace.name` a published artifact on AH? Should there be a warning that the installed version that the collection didn't have the expected manifest file?
@geerlingguy The fix for this issue does suppress the warning for `ansible-galaxy collection install` as well.

@geerlingguy Turns out that #68925 didn't actually fix the warning during installation though I swear I tested it (I blame my "first week back at work" brain 🤪). Anyway, the warning during installation should be fixed in #69541.

review_comments: I'm not sure if we want to support `galaxy.yaml` as well. We do that in certain places so it may be good to add that.

For ansible-doc this was added:
`lib/ansible/collections/__init__.py:B_FLAG_FILES = frozenset([b'MANIFEST.json', b'galaxy.yml'])`

I think we could just centralize usage here (or even move to constants.py) in case of future expansion (shocked no one has insisted on galaxy.yaml yet)

@samdoran I don't see `galaxy.yaml` supported anywhere for `ansible-galaxy collection` yet. Maybe it should be implemented in a separate PR though, so that it can be added for `build` at the same time rather than piecemeal.

@bcoca +1 to centralizing

@s-hertel I may have just imagined it, or maybe I saw this in `execute_install()` https://github.com/ansible/ansible/blob/25c5388fdec9e56517a93feb5e8d485680946c25/lib/ansible/cli/galaxy.py#L1021-L1021

Anyway, this should be a separate PR and centralized.
